translations.idiomatic: Yet you, sir, steep yourself in the Way and polish your arts, stand like a silent peak, your hidden insight probes the subtle, your reading runs deep, you toil nights without thought of sleep and spend days probing mysteries, year on year, never swerving from your purpose.

sentences.zh: 鱗翼成而愈伏，術業優而不試。

translations.literal: Scales and wings complete yet more you crouch; craft and learning excellent yet not tried.
translations.idiomatic: Though your talent has grown fins and feathers, you bury it deeper; though your learning surpasses others, you refuse to test it in office.

sentences.zh: 乃欲闔櫝辭價，泥蟠深處，永戢琳琅之耀，匿首窮魚之渚，當唐年而慕長沮，邦有道而反甯武。

translations.literal: Then you desire to shut the box and decline price, mud-coil in a deep place, forever sheathe luster of fine jade, hide head in the islet of exhausted fish; facing Tang years you admire Changju, state having the Way you reverse toward Ningwu.
translations.idiomatic: You would lock away your talents like jewels in a casket, lie coiled in the mud, forever dim the gleam of your gifts, and hide like a spent fish in a shoal—envying Changju under the sage kings of Yao and Shun, yet imitating Ningwu when the realm is well governed.

sentences.zh: 識彼迷此，愚竊不取。

translations.literal: To know that and be lost on this—stupid I privately do not take.
translations.idiomatic: To praise that course while blundering on this—such folly I cannot accept.

sentences.zh: 若乃士以援登，進必待求，附勢之黨橫擢，則林藪之彥不抽，丹墀步紈誇之童，東野遺白顛之叟。

translations.literal: As for gentlemen by pull ascending, advance must await seeking; when parties attached to power are promoted across the board, then forest-and-marsh's outstanding men are not drawn forth; vermillion steps walk silk-boasting boys; eastern wilds leave white-headed old men.
translations.idiomatic: When office goes only to the well-connected and promotion waits on solicitation, cliques of the powerful monopolize advancement while recluses of talent stay hidden—boys in silks swagger up the palace stairs while white-haired worthies are left in the eastern wilds.

sentences.zh: 盍亦因數都而事博陸，憑鷁首以涉洪流，蹈翠雲以駭逸龍，振光耀以驚沈鰌。

translations.literal: Why not also rely on the capital and serve the Marquis of Bolu, borrow goose prow to cross the rushing current, tread emerald clouds to startle roaming dragons, shake radiance to alarm sunken loach?
translations.idiomatic: Why not seize your moment at court, ride the wake of a Huo Guang, skim the flood on a high prow, tread the clouds to rouse soaring dragons, and flash your light to stir the depths?

sentences.zh: 徒屈蟠于陷井，眄天路而不遊，學既積而身困，夫何為乎秘丘。

translations.literal: In vain you coil in a pitfall, gaze at heaven's road and do not roam; learning already piled yet the body trapped—what do you do in a secret hill?
translations.idiomatic: Why coil in a snare, eyes on the high road yet never walking it—learning heaped up while the man stays stuck? What is the use of a hermit's hill?

sentences.zh: 且歲不我與，時若奔駟，有來無反，難得易失。

translations.literal: Moreover the years do not wait for me; the seasons are like galloping teams; they come and do not return; hard to obtain, easy to lose.
translations.idiomatic: Time does not wait; the seasons race like chariots—what comes does not return, hard to win and easy to lose.

sentences.zh: 先生不知盱豫之讖悔遲，而忘夫朋盍之義務疾，亦豈能登海湄而抑東流之水，臨虞泉而招西歸之日？

translations.literal: Sir, do you not know the omen of yu-yu's regret for lateness, and forget the duty of friends-together's haste for speed—how then can you climb the sea's margin and dam the eastward-flowing water, stand by the Yu spring and beckon the west-returning sun?
translations.idiomatic: Sir, do you miss the lesson of dithering until regret is too late, and ignore how allies must act with speed—do you think you can stand at the ocean's edge and stem the eastern tide, or by a sunless pool summon the setting sun back west?

sentences.zh: 徒以曲畏為梏，儒學自桎，囚大道於環堵，苦形骸於蓬室。

translations.literal: In vain you take crooked fear as fetters, Confucian learning self-shackles, imprison the great Way within a ringed wall, bitterly shape the body in a thatched room.
translations.idiomatic: You let needless fear bind you, let book learning become your cage, lock the great Way inside a cramped lane, and torment your frame in a mean hut.

sentences.zh: 豈若托身權戚，憑勢假力，擇棲芳林，飛不待翼，夕宿七娥之房，朝享五鼎之食，匡三正則太階平，贊五教而玉繩直。

translations.literal: How does that compare to entrusting the body to power and kin, borrowing force from position, choosing roost in fragrant woods, flying without awaiting wings, evening lodging in the rooms of the seven beauties, morning enjoying the food of five tripods, rectifying the three norms then the Grand Step is level, assisting the five teachings then the jade cord is straight?
translations.idiomatic: Better to shelter under great houses, ride influence and borrowed strength, perch in the high forest, soar without waiting for wings, sup in mansions of delight, feast from bronze vessels, set the three norms aright so the stairway of state is level, and further the five teachings so the celestial cord hangs true—

sentences.zh: 孰若茹藿餐蔬，終身自匿哉！」

translations.literal: Who compares to eating bean-leaves and coarse greens, to the end concealing oneself!"
translations.idiomatic: who would rather gnaw herbs in hiding for life?"

sentences.zh: 束子曰：「居！

translations.literal: Master Shu said: "Sit!"
translations.idiomatic: Shu Xi said, "Sit down."

sentences.zh: 吾將導爾以君子之道，諭爾以出處之事。

translations.literal: I will guide you with the gentleman's Way, instruct you in the affairs of emerging and dwelling.
translations.idiomatic: I shall set before you the way of the gentleman and explain what it means to serve or to withdraw.

sentences.zh: 爾其明受餘訊，謹聽餘志。

translations.literal: You there, brightly receive my questioning; carefully listen to my intent.
translations.idiomatic: Listen closely to my questions and attend carefully to what I mean to say.

sentences.zh: 昔元一既啟，兩儀肇立，離光夜隱，望舒晝戢，羽族翔林，蟩蛁赴濕，物從性之所安，士樂志之所執，或背豐榮以岩棲，或排蘭闥而求入，在野者龍逸，在朝者鳳集。

translations.literal: Formerly the Primordial One already opened, the Two Forms began to stand; Li's light hid at night, the Moon-charioteer folded by day; feathered tribes soar in forests; caterpillars and larvae hurry to damp; things follow what nature settles in; gentlemen delight in what ambition grasps; some turn back from rich glory to dwell on cliffs; some push aside orchid gates to seek entry; those in the wilds are dragons in flight; those at court are phoenixes gathered.
translations.idiomatic: When primordial unity first opened and yin and yang took shape, the sun hid its light at night and the moon yielded the day to birds winging through the woods and worms hastening to moisture—each creature follows its nature, each gentleman his chosen aim. Some spurn splendor for a life on the crags; others thrust aside palace gates to enter service. Recluses are dragons in flight; courtiers are phoenixes alighting.

sentences.zh: 雖其軌跡不同，而道無貴賤，必安其業，交不相羨，稷、契奮庸以宣道，巢、由洗耳以避禪，同垂不朽之稱，俱入賢者之流。

translations.literal: Although their tracks differ, in the Way there is no noble or base; they must pacify their occupation; they mutually do not envy; Ji and Qi rose to employments to proclaim the Way; Chao and You washed ears to avoid yielding the throne; together they hang the title of imperishable; both enter the stream of the worthy.
translations.idiomatic: Their paths diverge, yet in the Way itself there is no high or low—each must rest content in his calling and not covet another's. Ji and Qi took office to spread the teaching; Chao and You washed their ears rather than accept the throne—both won an undying name and both rank among the worthy.

sentences.zh: 參名比譽，誰劣誰優？

translations.literal: Join names and compare reputations—who is inferior, who is superior?
translations.idiomatic: Set name beside name and fame beside fame—who falls short, who excels?

sentences.zh: 何必貪與二八為群，而恥為七人之疇乎！

translations.literal: Why must one be greedy to be grouped with the two-eight, and ashamed to be a mate of the seven men!
translations.idiomatic: Why crave a place among the eight sage ministers and scorn standing with the seven recluses!

sentences.zh: 且道睽而通，士不同趣，吾竊綴處者之末行，未敢聞子之高喻，將忽蒲輪而不眄，夫何權戚之雲附哉！

translations.literal: Moreover the Way parts yet penetrates; gentlemen do not share one inclination; I privately stitch myself to the tail conduct of those who dwell in retirement; I dare not hear your high analogy; I am about to ignore the rush-wheeled summons and not glance at it—what then is this talk of attaching to power and kin!
translations.idiomatic: The Way may fork yet still meet; men of worth need not share one taste. I count myself among the humblest recluses and cannot accept your lofty comparison—I would pass by even a coach sent in earnest summons—so what is this about clinging to the mighty?

sentences.zh: 昔周、漢中衰，時難自托，福兆既開，患端亦作，朝游巍峨之宮，夕墜崢嶸之壑，晝笑夜歎，晨華暮落，忠不足以衛己，禍不可以預度，是士諱登朝而競赴林薄。

translations.literal: Formerly Zhou and Han middle declined; the times were hard to entrust oneself to; omens of blessing already opened, openings of disaster also arose; morning they roamed towering palaces, evening they fell into jagged ravines; daytime laugh, night sigh; morning flower, evening fall; loyalty was not sufficient to guard oneself; disaster could not be measured beforehand; therefore gentlemen shunned ascending court and raced to forest and thicket.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhou and Han slid into decline, the age was treacherous: good fortune opened its door, but calamity waited too—men who breakfasted in lofty halls might sup in jagged gorges, laughing by day and groaning by night, blooming at dawn and withering at dusk. Loyalty could not shield you; disaster struck without warning. That is why men of honor shunned the capital and fled to the wilds.

sentences.zh: 或毀名自汙，或不食其祿，比從政於匣笥之龜，譬官者於郊廟之犢，公孫泣涕而辭相，楊雄抗論於赤族。

translations.literal: Some destroyed name and defiled themselves; some did not eat their salaries; compare it to taking office from the casketed tortoise; liken holding office to the calf at suburban temples; Gongsun wept tears and declined the chancellorship; Yang Xiong raised argument against the red-clan.
translations.idiomatic: Some ruined their good name to save their skins; others refused stipends from a discredited throne—no better than letting a temple tortoise choose your career, or like the sacrificial calf led to the suburban altars. Gongsun Hong wept as he declined the chancellorship; Yang Xiong spoke out against courting the executioner's axe.

sentences.zh: 今大晉熙隆，六合寧靜。

translations.literal: Now the great Jin is bright and high; the six harmonies are tranquil and still.
translations.idiomatic: Today Great Jin flourishes in peace; the realm within the four seas is calm.

sentences.zh: 蜂蠆止毒，熊羆輟猛，五刑勿用，八紘備整，主無驕肆之怒，臣無犛纓之請，上下相安，率禮從道。

translations.literal: Hornets and scorpions stop venom; bears and brown bears cease fierceness; the five punishments are not used; the eight cords are fully ordered; the lord has no arrogant excess's anger; ministers have no yak-tail tassel's requests; above and below mutually are at peace; they follow ritual and follow the Way.
translations.idiomatic: Stings of malice are stilled, the fierceness of bears is checked, punishments lie unused, and the far reaches are ordered; the ruler does not rage at whim, ministers do not angle for dangling tassels of rank; high and low dwell in harmony under rite and principle.

sentences.zh: 朝養觸邪之獸，庭有指佞之草，禍戮可以忠逃，寵祿可以順保。

translations.literal: The court nurtures the beast that gores the crooked; the courtyard has the grass that points at flattery; disaster and execution can be escaped by loyalty; favor and salary can be preserved by compliance.
translations.idiomatic: The court keeps the straight-horned beast that gores the wicked, and the courtyard grows the plant that betrays sycophants—loyalty wards off ruin, and orderly conduct secures honor and pay.

sentences.zh: 且夫進無險懼，而惟寂之務者，率其性也。

translations.literal: Moreover, for advancing without perilous fear, while only taking stillness's tasks—such follows his nature.
translations.idiomatic: Besides, to advance without dread of danger yet cleave to a life of quiet—that is simply following one's nature.

sentences.zh: 兩可俱是，而舍彼趣此者，從其志也。

translations.literal: When both can both be right, yet abandoning that and rushing to this—such follows his will.
translations.idiomatic: When either course may be justified, yet one turns from that and chooses this—that is following one's own bent.

sentences.zh: 蓋無為可以解天下之紛，澹泊可以救國家之急，當位者事有所窮，陳策者言有不入，翟璜不能回西鄰之寇，平、勃不能正如意之立，幹木臥而秦師退，四皓起而戚姬泣。

translations.literal: In general non-action can untie the realm's below's tangles; blandness can save the state's urgency; those in position have affairs that reach exhaustion; those who set forth plans have words that do not enter; Di Huang could not turn back the western neighbor's raiders; Ping and Bo could not rectify Ruyi's installation; Ganmu lay down and Qin armies withdrew; the Four Hoary Ones rose and Lady Qi wept.
translations.idiomatic: Nonaction can unravel the empire's knots; quiet simplicity can meet a state's crisis. Even those in power meet limits; even good counsel may not get a hearing. Di Huang could not stop the raid from the west; Chen Ping and Zhou Bo could not set the heir-apparent question right; Duan Ganmu stayed in bed and the Qin host drew back; the Four Hoary Ones came forth and Lady Qi wept her doom.

sentences.zh: 夫如是何舍何執，何去何就？

translations.literal: If it is thus, what abandoning what grasping, what going what approaching?
translations.idiomatic: Given that, what is there to renounce or cling to, to flee or pursue?

sentences.zh: 謂山岑之林為芳，穀底之莽為臭。

translations.literal: Calling the forest on a mountain peak fragrant, calling the weeds at the valley bottom stinking.
translations.idiomatic: You call a grove on the heights fragrant and rank growth in the hollows foul—

sentences.zh: 守分任性，唯天所授，鳥不假甲於龜，魚不借足於獸，何必笑孤竹之貧而羨齊景之富！

translations.literal: Guarding allotment and following nature, only Heaven grants; birds do not borrow armor from tortoises; fish do not borrow feet from beasts; why must one laugh at Guzhu's poverty and envy Duke Jing of Qi's wealth!
translations.idiomatic: yet each keeps his portion and follows his endowment—birds do not borrow shells from turtles, fish do not borrow legs from beasts. Why mock the poor integrity of the Guzhu brothers and covet the riches of Duke Jing of Qi?

sentences.zh: 恥布衣以肆志，甯文裘而拖繡。

translations.literal: Ashamed of plain cloth thereby to give free rein to intent; rather patterned hide and trailing embroidery.
translations.idiomatic: Better to feel shame in plain cloth while following your heart than to trail embroidered furs in moral compromise.

sentences.zh: 且能約其躬，則儋石之畜以豐；

translations.literal: Moreover if one can restrain one's person, then a dan-shi store becomes abundant;
translations.idiomatic: Keep the body in check, and a modest granary feels full;

sentences.zh: 苟肆其欲，則海陵之積不足；

translations.literal: if one wantonly releases one's desires, then Hailing's piled stores are not sufficient;
translations.idiomatic: give free rein to appetite, and even the granaries of Hailing would not suffice;

sentences.zh: 存道德者，則匹夫之身可榮；

translations.literal: those who preserve the Way and power, then the body of a common man can be glorious;
translations.idiomatic: hold fast to virtue, and a commoner's life shines bright;

sentences.zh: 忘大倫者，則萬乘之主猶辱。

translations.literal: those who forget the great human relationships, then even the lord of ten thousand chariots still is disgraced.
translations.idiomatic: forget the great bonds of humanity, and even a ruler of ten thousand chariots stands dishonored.

sentences.zh: 將研六籍以訓世，守寂泊以鎮俗，偶鄭老於海隅，匹嚴叟於僻蜀。

translations.literal: I will grind the six canons to instruct the age, guard stillness and blandness to press down the vulgar, pair with Zheng the old at the sea's corner, match Yan the elder in remote Shu.
translations.idiomatic: I mean to study the Six Classics to instruct the world, keep to quiet simplicity to steady common ways, and keep company with old Zheng by the shore and recluse Yan in distant Shu.

sentences.zh: 且世乙太虛為輿，玄爐為肆，神游莫競之林，心存無營之室，榮利不擾其覺，殷憂不幹其寐，捐誇者之所貪，收躁務之所棄，雉聖籍之荒蕪，總群言之一至。

translations.literal: Moreover, taking the Grand Void as carriage, the dark furnace as market, spirit roams in the forest of none who rival, mind dwells in the chamber of none who schemes; glory and profit do not disturb his waking, deep sorrow does not interfere with his sleep; he casts away what boasters crave, gathers what restless affairs discard; clears the wilderness of the sage canons, gathers the crowd of words to one arrival.
translations.idiomatic: I would take boundless void for my chariot and the hidden forge for my stall, roam in tracts where no rival intrudes, and lodge where no schemes stir—unmoved by gain in waking hours, untroubled by care in sleep, leaving to the vain what they chase, reclaiming what the frantic cast aside, clearing the neglected ground of the classics, and bringing many voices to a single insight.

sentences.zh: 全素履於丘園，背纓緌而長逸，請子課吾業於千載，無聽吾言於今日也。」

translations.literal: He completes plain walking in hill and garden, turns back tassel-cords and long flees; you, sir, examine my occupation in a thousand years; do not listen to my words today."
translations.idiomatic: I would keep plain integrity in field and grove, turn my back on official cords, and wander far—judge my life's work a millennium hence, not by what I say today."

sentences.zh: 張華見而奇之。

translations.literal: Zhang Hua saw it and deemed him strange.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Hua read it and was struck by his talent.

sentences.zh: 石鑒卒，王戎乃辟璆。

translations.literal: When Shi Jian died, Wang Rong then summoned Qiu.
translations.idiomatic: After Shi Jian died, Wang Rong at last offered Qiu a post.

sentences.zh: 華召晳為掾，又為司空、下邳王晃所辟。

translations.literal: Hua summoned Xi to be a retainer; moreover he was summoned by the Minister of Works, Prince of Xiapi, Huang.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Hua appointed Xi as a clerk, and he was also recruited by Prince Huang of Xiapi, who held the post of Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 華為司空，復以為賊曹屬。

translations.literal: When Hua became Minister of Works, again he made him Banditry Section subordinate.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Hua became Minister of Works, he again named Xi an aide in the section for bandit suppression.

sentences.zh: 時欲廣農，晳上議曰：轉佐著作郎，撰《晉書·帝紀》、十《志》，遷轉博士，著作如故。

translations.literal: At the time wishing to broaden agriculture, Xi submitted a memorial saying: he was transferred to assistant editorial director, compiled the Jin History annals and the ten treatises, was transferred to erudite, and his editorial duties remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: When the court wanted to promote farming, Shu Xi offered policy advice; he was then made assistant director of composition, tasked with drafting the dynastic annals and ten monographs of the Jin History, promoted to academician, and kept his editorial post.

sentences.zh: 初，，汲郡人不准盜發魏襄王墓，或言安釐王塚，得竹書數十車。

translations.literal: In the beginning, a man of Ji commandery named Bu Zhun robbed open the tomb of King Xiang of Wei, or some say the mound of King Ai of An, and obtained several cartloads of bamboo documents.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Bu Zhun of Ji commandery broke into the tomb of King Xiang of Wei—some identify it as the burial of King Ai of An—and hauled out dozens of cartloads of bamboo texts.

sentences.zh: 其《紀年》十三篇，記夏以來至周幽王為犬戎所滅，以事接之，三家分，仍述魏事至安釐王之二十年。

translations.literal: Among them the Bamboo Annals in thirteen sections records from Xia down to King You of Zhou destroyed by the Dog Rong, joins events to it, the three houses divided Jin, and still narrates Wei affairs down to the twentieth year of King Ai.
translations.idiomatic: Its Bamboo Annals, in thirteen fascicles, runs from the Xia down through King You of Zhou, overrun by the Dog Rong, carries the story into the partition among the three great houses, and continues Wei history to the twentieth year of King Ai.

sentences.zh: 蓋魏國之史書，大略與《春秋》皆多相應。

translations.literal: It was broadly the historical writings of the state of Wei; in large outline they largely corresponded with the Spring and Autumn Annals.
translations.idiomatic: These were essentially Wei state annals that, in the main, align closely with the Spring and Autumn.

sentences.zh: 其中經傳大異，則雲夏年多殷；

translations.literal: Among them where classic and commentary greatly differed, then it said the Xia calendar had more years than the Yin.
translations.idiomatic: Where its record diverges sharply from received classics, it claims the Xia reign count exceeds that of the Shang.

sentences.zh: 益幹啟位，啟殺之；

translations.literal: Yi interfered with Qi's position; Qi killed him.
translations.idiomatic: Yi usurped Qi's throne; Qi had him killed.

sentences.zh: 太甲殺伊尹；

translations.literal: Taijia killed Yi Yin.
translations.idiomatic: King Taijia executed Yi Yin.

sentences.zh: 文丁殺季曆；

translations.literal: Wen Ding killed Ji Li.
translations.idiomatic: King Wen Ding put Ji Li to death.

sentences.zh: 自周受命，至穆王百年，非穆王壽百歲也；

translations.literal: From the Zhou receiving the mandate down to King Mu was one hundred years; it is not that King Mu's lifespan was one hundred years.
translations.idiomatic: It counts a century from Zhou's receipt of the mandate to King Mu—not a claim that King Mu lived a hundred years.

sentences.zh: 幽王既亡，有共伯和者攝行天子事，非二相共和也。

translations.literal: After King You had perished, there was Gong Bo He who acted in the Son of Heaven's affairs; it was not the two ministers' joint rule called 'harmony.'
translations.idiomatic: After King You fell, Gong Bo He held the regency; this is not the 'joint harmony' regency of two ministers in received tradition.

sentences.zh: 其《易經》二篇，與《周易》上下經同。

translations.literal: Its Changes Classic in two sections was the same as the Zhou Changes upper and lower classics.
translations.idiomatic: Its two-part Changes matches the upper and lower wings of the Zhou Changes.

sentences.zh: 《易繇陰陽卦》二篇，與《周易》略同，《繇辭》則異。

translations.literal: The Changes of Yin and Yang Hexagrams in two sections was largely the same as the Zhou Changes, but the oracle texts differed.
translations.idiomatic: The two scrolls of Yin-Yang line statements largely parallel the Zhou Changes, though the line texts diverge.

sentences.zh: 《卦下易經》一篇，似《說卦》而異。

translations.literal: The Changes Classic beneath the Hexagrams in one piece resembled Explaining the Hexagrams but differed.
translations.idiomatic: One scroll of sub-hexagram commentary resembles the Explaining the Hexagrams yet is not identical.

sentences.zh: 《公孫段》二篇，公孫段與邵陟論《易》。

translations.literal: Gongsun Duan in two sections: Gongsun Duan and Shao Zhi discussed the Changes.
translations.idiomatic: Two scrolls titled Gongsun Duan record a dialogue on the Changes between Gongsun Duan and Shao Zhi.

sentences.zh: 《國語》三篇，言楚、晉事。

translations.literal: Discourses of the States in three sections spoke of Chu and Jin affairs.
translations.idiomatic: A three-part Discourses of the States treats events in Chu and Jin.

sentences.zh: 《名》三篇，似《禮記》，又似《爾雅》《論語》。

translations.literal: The Names in three sections resembled the Record of Rites, and also resembled the Erya and the Analects.
translations.idiomatic: A three-part Names recalls both the Record of Rites and compendia in the vein of the Erya and Analects.

sentences.zh: 《師春》一篇，書《左傳》諸卜筮，「師春」似是造書者姓名也。

translations.literal: Shichun in one piece wrote the various divinations of the Zuo Tradition; 'Shichun' seems to be the name of the person who made the book.
translations.idiomatic: Shichun collects the Zuo Tradition's divination episodes; the title probably preserves the compiler's name.

sentences.zh: 《瑣語》十一篇，諸國卜夢妖怪相書也。

translations.literal: Trivial Sayings in eleven sections was the book of the various states' dream divinations, prodigies, and physiognomy.
translations.idiomatic: Eleven fascicles of Trivial Sayings compile dream omens, anomalies, and physiognomy lore from many states.

sentences.zh: 《梁丘藏》一篇，先敘魏之世數，次言丘藏金玉事。

translations.literal: Liangqiu Zang in one piece first narrated the generations of Wei, next spoke of hill-hoard gold and jade matters.
translations.idiomatic: Liangqiu Zang opens with Wei reign chronology, then turns to buried treasure in hill vaults.

sentences.zh: 《繳書》二篇，論弋射法。

translations.literal: Corded-arrow Writings in two sections discussed the method of corded-arrow shooting.
translations.idiomatic: Two scrolls on corded-arrow archery spell out the technique.

sentences.zh: 《生封》一篇，帝王所封。

translations.literal: Shengfeng in one piece was what emperors enfeoffed.
translations.idiomatic: Shengfeng lists imperial enfeoffments.

sentences.zh: 《大曆》二篇，鄒子談天類也。

translations.literal: Great Calendar in two sections was of the kind of Master Zou discoursing on heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Great Calendar, in two parts, belongs with cosmological writings in the tradition of Zou Yan.

sentences.zh: 《穆天子傳》五篇，言周穆王遊行四海，見帝台、西王母。

translations.literal: Tradition of King Mu of Zhou in five sections spoke of King Mu of Zhou roaming the four seas, seeing Di Tai and the Queen Mother of the West.
translations.idiomatic: Five scrolls of the King Mu tradition describe his tour of the realm and meetings with Di Tai and the Queen Mother of the West.

sentences.zh: 《圖詩》一篇，畫贊之屬也。

translations.literal: Illustrated Poems in one piece belonged to the kind of painted eulogies.
translations.idiomatic: Illustrated Poems is a gallery-style verse cycle with captions.

sentences.zh: 又雜書十九篇：《周食田法》，《周書》，《論楚事》，《周穆王美人盛姬死事》。

translations.literal: Also miscellaneous writings nineteen pieces: Zhou Field-allotment Law, Zhou Documents, Discussing Chu Affairs, Affair of the Death of King Mu of Zhou's Beautiful Lady Sheng Ji.
translations.idiomatic: Another nineteen miscellaneous works include Zhou field law, Zhou state papers, essays on Chu, and the death of King Mu's consort Sheng Ji.

sentences.zh: 大凡七十五篇，七篇簡書折壞，不識名題。

translations.literal: In all seventy-five sections; seven bamboo bundles were broken, their titles not known.
translations.idiomatic: Seventy-five titles survive in all; seven damaged bundles could not be identified.

sentences.zh: 塚中又得銅劍一枚，長二尺五寸。

translations.literal: From the tomb they also obtained one bronze sword, length two chi five cun.
translations.idiomatic: The diggers also pulled out a bronze sword two and a half feet long.

sentences.zh: 漆書皆科斗字。

translations.literal: The lacquer writing was all tadpole characters.
translations.idiomatic: The lacquered slips were all in tadpole seal script.

sentences.zh: 初發塚者燒策照取寶物，及官收之，多燼簡斷劄，文既殘缺，不復詮次。

translations.literal: At first those who opened the tomb burned slips to shine and take treasures; when officials collected them, many were burnt slips and broken slips; the text being already incomplete, they could no longer arrange the order.
translations.idiomatic: Looters first torched slips for light while plundering treasure, so when officials recovered the haul much was charred or snapped; the text was too fragmentary to restore original order.

sentences.zh: 武帝以其書付秘書校綴次第，尋考指歸，而以今文寫之。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu handed the documents to the Palace Library to collate sequence, investigate point and return, and write them in current script.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu entrusted the slips to the imperial library for collation, interpretation, and transcription into regular script.

sentences.zh: 晳在著作，得觀竹書，隨疑分釋，皆有義證。

translations.literal: Xi while in the composition post was able to view the bamboo documents; following doubts he split and explained them; all had reasoned verification.
translations.idiomatic: As an editorial scribe, Shu Xi could study the cache and produced well-argued clarifications wherever the text was obscure.

sentences.zh: 遷尚書郎。

translations.literal: He was promoted to gentleman of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to secretary in the imperial secretariat.

sentences.zh: 武帝嘗問摯虞三日曲水之義，虞對曰：「漢章帝時，平原徐肇以三月初生三女，至三日俱亡，村人以為怪，乃招攜之水濱洗祓，遂因水以泛觴，其義起此。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu once asked Zhi Yu the meaning of the third-day curved-water gathering; Yu replied: 'In the time of Han Zhangdi, Pingyuan Xu Zhao on the third of the third month bore three daughters; by the third day all had died; the villagers thought it strange, then led them to the water's edge to wash and exorcise; therefore by the water they floated goblets; its meaning began here.'
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu once asked Zhi Yu why courtiers held the spring outing with floating cups along a winding channel. Zhi Yu traced it to Han Zhangdi's reign, when Xu Zhao of Pingyuan bore triplets on the third day of the third month and lost all three by the feast day; neighbors led the family to the river for purification, then set cups adrift on the current—so the custom began, he said.

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「必如所談，便非好事。

translations.literal: The emperor said: 'If it must be as you have spoken, then it is not a good affair.'
translations.idiomatic: The emperor replied, 'If that origin is true, the rite rests on ill omen, not merit.'

sentences.zh: 」晳進曰：「虞小生，不足以知，臣請言之。

translations.literal: Xi stepped forward and said: 'Yu is a young student, not sufficient to know; your servant begs to speak of it.'
translations.idiomatic: Shu Xi interjected: 'Zhi Yu is too junior to settle this; allow me to answer.'

sentences.zh: 昔周公成洛邑，因流水以泛酒，故逸詩云『羽觴隨波』。

translations.literal: Anciently the Duke of Zhou completed Luoyi; by flowing water he floated wine; therefore a lost poem says: "Feather goblets follow the waves."
translations.idiomatic: When the Duke of Zhou finished Luoyang, he already drifted cups on a winding stream—a lost ode speaks of goblets riding the ripples.

sentences.zh: 又秦昭王以三日置酒河曲，見金人奉水心之劍，曰：『令君制有西夏。

translations.literal: Also King Zhao of Qin on the third day set wine at the river bend, saw a golden man presenting a sword from the heart of the water, saying: 'Order you, lord, to control Western Xia.'
translations.idiomatic: King Zhao of Qin likewise feasted by a bend on the third day, saw a golden figure offer a sword from midstream, and heard the pledge that the ruler would master the western regions.

sentences.zh: 』乃霸諸侯，因此立為曲水。

translations.literal: Then he hegemoned the feudal lords; because of this it was established as curved water.
translations.idiomatic: He went on to lord it over the lords, and the winding-stream banquet became a precedent for power.

sentences.zh: 二漢相緣，皆為盛集。

translations.literal: The two Han continued it; all were grand gatherings.
translations.idiomatic: Both Western and Eastern Han kept the custom, always as splendid court festivals.

sentences.zh: 」帝大悅，賜晳金五十斤。

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly pleased and bestowed on Xi fifty jin of gold.
translations.idiomatic: Delighted, the emperor awarded Shu Xi fifty jin of gold.

sentences.zh: 時有人于嵩高山下得竹簡一枚，上兩行科斗書，傳以相示，莫有知者。

translations.literal: At the time someone below Songgao Mountain obtained one bamboo slip; on it two lines of tadpole writing; they passed it around to show one another; none knew it.
translations.idiomatic: Someone then found a single slip below Mount Song with two lines of tadpole script; it circulated among scholars, but no one could read it.

sentences.zh: 司空張華以問晳，晳曰：「此漢明帝顯節陵中策文也。

translations.literal: Minister of Works Zhang Hua used it to ask Xi; Xi said: 'This is the tomb-strategy text from Emperor Ming of Han's Xianjie mausoleum.'
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Hua, as minister of works, showed it to Shu Xi, who identified it as a burial inscription from Emperor Ming's Xianjie tomb.

sentences.zh: 」檢驗果然，時人伏其博識。

translations.literal: Inspection verified it was so; people of the time submitted to his broad learning.
translations.idiomatic: Archives confirmed his reading, and contemporaries marveled at his erudition.

sentences.zh: 趙王倫為相國，請為記室。

translations.literal: Prince Zhao Lun was chancellor of state and requested him to be secretary in the headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Zhao Lun served as chief minister, he tried to appoint Shu Xi chief secretary of his staff.

sentences.zh: 晳辭疾罷歸，教授門徒。

translations.literal: Xi declined citing illness, resigned and returned, and taught disciples.
translations.idiomatic: Shu Xi pleaded illness, went home, and taught private students.

sentences.zh: 年四十卒，元城市裏為之廢業，門生故人立碑墓側。

translations.literal: He died at forty; the market ward of Yuancheng city for him ceased work; disciples and old friends erected a stele beside the tomb.
translations.idiomatic: He died at forty; trades in Yuancheng's market suspended business in mourning; pupils and friends set up a stone by his grave.

sentences.zh: 晳才學博通，所著《三魏人士傳》，《七代通記》、《晉書·紀》、《志》，遇亂亡失。

translations.literal: Xi's talents and learning broadly penetrated; what he wrote—Records of Worthies of the Three Weis, Comprehensive Record of Seven Dynasties, Jin Annals and Treatises—met turmoil and was lost.
translations.idiomatic: Shu Xi was encyclopedic, but his Records of Wei Notables, Seven Dynasties Digest, and drafts of the Jin annals and monographs perished in the wars.

sentences.zh: 其《五經通論》、《發蒙記》、《補亡詩》、文集數十篇，行於世雲。

translations.literal: His Comprehensive Discussion of the Five Classics, Notes for Opening the Dark, Poems to Repair the Lost, and collected writings several tens of chapters moved in the world.
translations.idiomatic: His Five Classics synthesis, primer notes, supplement to the lost odes, and collected essays—several dozen scrolls—did circulate.

sentences.zh: 王接

translations.literal: Wang Jie
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jie

sentences.zh: 王接，字祖遊，河東猗氏人，漢京兆尹尊十世孫也。

translations.literal: Wang Jie, style Zuyou, was a man of Yishi in Hedong, tenth-generation descendant of Han capital intendant Wang Zun.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jie, courtesy Zuyou, came from Yishi in Hedong and was the tenth-generation heir of Wang Zun, metropolitan governor under Han.

sentences.zh: 父蔚，世修儒史之學。

translations.literal: His father Wei, for generations cultivated Confucian and historical learning.
translations.idiomatic: His father Wang Wei came from a long line of Confucian historians.

sentences.zh: 魏中領軍曹羲作《至公論》，蔚善之，而著《至機論》，辭義甚美。

translations.literal: Wei central army supervisor Cao Xi made the Treatise on Utmost Impartiality; Wei praised it and wrote the Treatise on Utmost Pivot; its phrasing and meaning were very fine.
translations.idiomatic: When Cao Xi, central army supervisor under Wei, wrote On Utmost Fairness, Wang Wei admired it and replied with On the Ultimate Pivot—an essay of rare polish.

sentences.zh: 官至夏陽侯相。

translations.literal: His office reached chancellor of the marquisate of Xiayang.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to magistrate-chancellor of the Xiayang marquisate.

sentences.zh: 接幼喪父，哀毀過禮，鄉親皆歎曰：「王氏有子哉！

translations.literal: Jie in youth lost his father; grief destroyed beyond the rites; villagers all sighed: 'The Wang clan has a son!'
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jie lost his father young and mourned past what ritual prescribed; neighbors exclaimed that the Wangs had raised a worthy heir.

sentences.zh: 」渤海劉原為河東太守，好奇，以旌才為務。

translations.literal: Liu Yuan of Bohai was Hedong grand warden; he loved the strange and took displaying talent as his task.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yuan of Bohai, as Hedong governor, cultivated odd talents and made a point of promoting them.

sentences.zh: 同郡馮收試經為郎，七十餘，薦接于原曰：「夫驊騮不總轡，則非造父之肆；

translations.literal: Feng Shou of the same commandery tested the classics to become a gentleman; over seventy; he recommended Jie to Yuan, saying: 'If fine steeds do not have the reins gathered, then it is not Zaofu's stable.'
translations.idiomatic: Feng Shou of the same commandery, a classics graduate in his seventies, urged Liu Yuan: 'A team unhitched is no chariot for Zaofu.'

sentences.zh: 明月不流光，則非隋侯之掌。

translations.literal: If the bright moon does not cast flowing light, then it is not in the Marquis of Sui's palm.
translations.idiomatic: A moonbeam withheld is no pearl in the Marquis of Sui's hand.

sentences.zh: 伏惟明府苞黃中之德，耀重離之明，求賢與能，小無遺錯，是以鄙老思獻所知。

translations.literal: I humbly consider that the enlightened prefect embraces the virtue of the yellow center, shines the brightness of layered li, seeks worthies and the able, and in small things has no oversight; therefore this lowly old man wishes to present what he knows.
translations.idiomatic: Your honor unites inner strength with outward clarity, misses no talent however slight, so this aged subject ventures a name you should hear.

sentences.zh: 竊見處士王接，岐嶷俊異，十三而孤，居喪盡禮，學過目而知，義觸類而長，斯玉鉉之妙味，經世之徽猷也。

translations.literal: Privately I see recluse Wang Jie, outstanding and sharp, at thirteen orphaned; in mourning he exhausted the rites; learning—on passing the eyes he knew; principles—touching categories he lengthened; this is the fine flavor of the jade handle, the emblematic plan for ordering the age.
translations.idiomatic: The recluse Wang Jie is precocious and keen: orphaned at thirteen yet scrupulous in mourning, he reads once and retains, and extends doctrine by analogy—true metal for the state's tripod, a design for governing the age.

sentences.zh: 不患玄黎之不啟，竊樂春英之及時。

translations.literal: Not worrying that the dark-haired masses will not awaken; privately I rejoice that spring's blossoms catch the season.
translations.idiomatic: I do not fear the people will stay blind to him; I rejoice that spring has brought its bloom in good time.

sentences.zh: 」原即禮命，接不受。

translations.literal: Yuan immediately with ritual summoned him; Jie did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yuan at once sent a formal summons; Wang Jie declined.

sentences.zh: 原乃呼見曰：「君欲慕肥遁之高邪？

translations.literal: Yuan then called him to a meeting and said: 'Do you wish to admire the height of fat reclusion?'
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yuan then had him brought in and asked whether he meant to rival the loftiest hermits.

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「接薄祜，少孤而無兄弟，母老疾篤，故無心為吏。

translations.literal: He replied: 'Jie's fate is thin in blessing; young orphaned and without brothers; mother old, illness heavy; therefore I have no heart to be a clerk.'
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jie answered that his life had been starved of fortune—orphaned early, brotherless, with an aged mother gravely ill—so office held no appeal.

sentences.zh: 」及母終，柴毀骨立，居墓次積年，備覽眾書，多出異義。

translations.literal: When his mother ended, he wasted from grief until bones stood; he dwelt by the tomb for years, thoroughly read the many books, and mostly produced divergent interpretations.
translations.idiomatic: After she died he wasted to the bone and lived at the graveside for years, reading widely and often dissenting from received glosses.

sentences.zh: 性簡率，不修俗操，鄉里大族多不能善之，唯裴頠雅知焉。

translations.literal: His nature was simple and direct; he did not cultivate vulgar deportment; great clans of the village mostly could not treat him well; only Pei Wei elegantly knew him.
translations.idiomatic: Plain and blunt, he scorned small-town polish, so local grandees disliked him—only Pei Wei truly understood him.

sentences.zh: 平陽太守柳澹、散騎侍郎裴遐、尚書僕射鄧攸皆與接友善。

translations.literal: Pingyang grand warden Liu Dan, scattered-cavalry attendant Pei Xia, and supervisor of the masters of writing Deng You all were friendly with Jie.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Dan, governor of Pingyang, attendant Pei Xia, and chief minister Deng You all counted him a friend.

sentences.zh: 後為郡主簿，迎太守溫宇，宇奇之，轉功曹史。

translations.literal: Later he became the county's principal clerk, welcomed Grand Warden Wen Yu; Yu thought him strange, transferred him to merit clerk.
translations.idiomatic: He later served as county recorder, impressed Governor Wen Yu on his arrival, and was moved to merit secretary.

sentences.zh: 州辟部平陽從事。

translations.literal: The province summoned him as Pingyang staff clerk.
translations.idiomatic: The provincial authorities then named him an aide on the Pingyang staff.

sentences.zh: 時泰山羊亮為平陽太守，薦之于司隸校尉王堪，出補都官從事。

translations.literal: At the time Taishan Yang Liang was Pingyang grand warden; he recommended him to metropolitan commandant Wang Kan; he issued supplement as capital-bandits clerk.
translations.idiomatic: When Yang Liang of Taishan governed Pingyang, he recommended Wang Jie to metropolitan commandant Wang Kan, who appointed him to the capital crimes section.

sentences.zh: 永甯初，舉秀才。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yongning, he was recommended as cultivated talent.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Yongning he was nominated as a recommended scholar.

sentences.zh: 友人滎陽潘滔遺接書曰：「摯虞、卞玄仁並謂足下應和鼎味，可無以應秀才行。

translations.literal: His friend Pan Tao of Yingchuan sent Jie a letter saying: 'Zhi Yu and Bian Xuanren both say your foot ought to harmonize the cauldron's taste—can you have nothing with which to answer for cultivated-talent conduct?'
translations.idiomatic: His friend Pan Tao wrote that Zhi Yu and Bian Xuanren expected him for high office—how could he ignore a summons to the cultivated-talent examination?

sentences.zh: 」接報書曰：「今世道交喪，將遂剝亂，而識智之士鉗口韜筆，禍敗日深，如火之燎原，其可救乎？

translations.literal: Jie answered in a letter: 'Now the generation's way is mutually lost; we are about to arrive at stripping chaos; while knowing wise men seal mouth and sheathe brush, disaster daily deepens like fire on the great plain—can it be saved?'
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jie replied that morals were collapsing toward outright pillage while thinkers sealed their lips; calamity spread like a prairie fire—what hope remained?

sentences.zh: 非榮斯行，欲極陳所見，冀有覺悟耳。

translations.literal: It is not for glory this conduct; I wish to exhaust stating what I have seen, hoping there may be awakening.
translations.idiomatic: He went not for glory but to speak his mind in the faint hope of waking the court.

sentences.zh: 」是歲，三王義舉，惠帝復阼，以國有大慶，天下秀孝一皆不試，接以為恨。

translations.literal: That year the three kings' righteous uprising; Emperor Hui restored the throne; because the state had a great celebration, all cultivated talents and filially recommended in the realm were each not tested; Jie took this as regret.
translations.idiomatic: That year the coalition of three princes restored Emperor Hui and proclaimed a general amnesty that waived examinations for every nominated scholar; Wang Jie resented missing his chance to argue policy.

sentences.zh: 除中郎，補征虜將軍司馬。

translations.literal: He was appointed gentleman of the center and supplemented as marshal to the general who subdues barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: He was named palace gentleman and adjunct marshal to the general who pacifies foreign foes.

sentences.zh: 蕩陰之役，侍中嵇紹為亂兵所害，接議曰：「夫謀人之軍，軍敗則死之；

translations.literal: At the Dangyin affair, attendant-in-ordinary Xi Shao was harmed by mutinous soldiers; Jie argued: 'When one plots another's army, when the army is defeated then die for it.'
translations.idiomatic: After Xi Shao died under rebel blades at Dangyin, Wang Jie argued that whoever shares command must share defeat.

sentences.zh: 謀人之國，國危則亡之，古之道也。

translations.literal: When one plots another's state, when the state is in peril then perish for it; it is the ancient way.
translations.idiomatic: Who shares responsibility for the realm must answer with his life when the realm totters—that was the classical rule.

sentences.zh: 蕩陰之役，百官奔北，唯嵇紹守職以遇不道，可謂臣矣，又可稱痛矣。

translations.literal: At the Dangyin affair the hundred officials fled north; only Xi Shao kept his post encountering the not-way; he can be called a minister; also he can be called a painful record.
translations.idiomatic: At Dangyin the court scattered in panic while Xi Shao alone held his ground against lawless troops—true ministerial fidelity and a tragedy worth recording.

sentences.zh: 今山東方欲大舉，宜明高節，以號令天下。

translations.literal: Now east of the mountains is about to raise a great movement; it is fitting to clarify high integrity in order to command the realm.
translations.idiomatic: With the eastern hosts readying a major campaign, the throne should exalt steadfast loyalty to rally the empire.

sentences.zh: 依《春秋》褒三累之義，加紹致命之賞，則遐邇向風，莫敢不肅矣。

translations.literal: According to the Spring and Autumn's meaning of honoring the threefold accumulation of merit, add to Shao the reward of laying down life; then far and near will turn to the wind; none will dare not be solemn.
translations.idiomatic: Citing the Annals' praise of cumulative merit, he urged posthumous honors for Xi Shao's martyrdom so every quarter would heed the lesson.

sentences.zh: 」朝廷從之。

translations.literal: The court followed it.
translations.idiomatic: The government adopted his recommendation.

sentences.zh: 河間王顒欲遷駕長安，與關東乖異，以接成都王佐，難之，表轉臨汾公相國。

translations.literal: Prince Yong of Hejian wished to move the imperial carriage to Chang'an; he differed with east of the passes; because Jie was Chengdu Prince's assistant, he found it difficult; he memorialized to transfer him to chancellor of the duke of Linfen.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Yong of Hejian, planning to shift the court to Chang'an against the eastern alliance, sidelined Chengdu Prince's aide Wang Jie by transferring him, on memorial, to chancellor of the duke of Linfen.

sentences.zh: 及東海王越率諸候討顒，尚書令王堪統行台，上請接補尚書殿中郎，未至而卒，年三十九。

translations.literal: When Prince of East Sea Yue led the feudal lords to attack Yong, supervisor of the masters of writing Wang Kan headed the mobile headquarters; upward he requested Jie supplement as gentleman of the palace section of the masters of writing; before he arrived he died, age thirty-nine.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Yue of the Eastern Sea marched against Yong, chief minister Wang Kan, commanding the field secretariat, tried to add Wang Jie as a palace-section secretary—Wang Jie died at thirty-nine before he could report.

sentences.zh: 接學雖博通，特精《禮》《傳》。

translations.literal: Though Jie's learning was broadly penetrating, he especially mastered the Rites and the commentaries.
translations.idiomatic: Erudite as he was, Wang Jie's deepest expertise lay in the ritual canon and its exegetical traditions.

sentences.zh: 常謂《左氏》辭義贍富，自是一家書，不主為經發。

translations.literal: He often said the Zuo Tradition's phrasing and meaning are rich; it is its own book; it does not chiefly act to issue the classic.
translations.idiomatic: He held that the Zuo narrative is self-sufficient literature rather than a mere gloss on the Spring and Autumn.

sentences.zh: 《公羊》附經立傳，經所不書，傳不妄起，于文為儉，通經為長。

translations.literal: The Gongyang attaches to the classic and sets commentary; what the classic does not write, the commentary does not recklessly begin; with regard to text it is economical; for penetrating the classic it is long.
translations.idiomatic: Gongyang, by contrast, hews to the classic: it never invents episodes the classic omits—spare in diction yet superior for unlocking the core text.

sentences.zh: 任城何休訓釋甚詳，而黜周王魯，大體乖硋，且志通《公羊》而往往還為《公羊》疾病。

translations.literal: Rencheng He Xiu's exegesis is very detailed, yet demotes Zhou and kings Lu—the great outline is contrary and obstructive; moreover his aim was to penetrate Gongyang, yet often in turn makes Gongyang's diseases.
translations.idiomatic: He Xiu of Rencheng is exhaustive yet demotes Zhou and elevates Lu, skewing the larger scheme; even while mastering Gongyang he often reproduces its faults.

sentences.zh: 接乃更注《公羊春秋》，多有新義。

translations.literal: Jie therefore again annotated the Gongyang Spring and Autumn; much had new meanings.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jie therefore re-annotated the Gongyang edition, offering many fresh readings.

sentences.zh: 時秘書丞衛恆考正汲塚書，未訖而遭難。

translations.literal: At the time secretariat assistant Wei Heng was examining and correcting the Ji tomb documents; not finished when he encountered disaster.
translations.idiomatic: While secretariat aide Wei Heng was still collating the tomb texts, he perished in the violence.

sentences.zh: 佐著作郎束皙述而成之，事多證異義。

translations.literal: Assistant editorial director Shu Xi narrated and completed it; matters often verified divergent meanings.
translations.idiomatic: Assistant director Shu Xi finished the project, often adjudicating disputed passages.

sentences.zh: 時東萊太守陳留王庭堅難之，亦有證據。

translations.literal: At the time Donglai grand warden Wang Tingjian of Chenliu disputed it; he also had evidence.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Tingjian of Chenliu, governor of Donglai, challenged the reconstruction with documentation of his own.

sentences.zh: 皙又釋難，而庭堅已亡。

translations.literal: Xi again explained the dispute; but Tingjian had already died.
translations.idiomatic: Shu Xi rebutted him, yet Wang Tingjian died before the debate closed.

sentences.zh: 散騎侍郎潘滔謂接曰：「卿才學理議，足解二子之紛，可試論之。

translations.literal: Scattered-cavalry attendant Pan Tao said to Jie: 'Your talents, learning, and reasoning are sufficient to untie the two gentlemen's quarrel; you may try to discuss it.'
translations.idiomatic: Pan Tao urged Wang Jie that his scholarship could settle the feud between Wei Heng's and Wang Tingjian's schools.

sentences.zh: 」接遂詳其得失。

translations.literal: Jie thereupon set out in detail their strengths and weaknesses.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jie then weighed each side's strengths and flaws in full detail.

sentences.zh: 摯虞、謝衡皆博物多聞，咸以為允當。

translations.literal: Zhi Yu and Xie Heng both broadly comprehended and broadly heard; all thought it appropriate.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi Yu and Xie Heng, both celebrated polymaths, judged his verdict sound.

sentences.zh: 又撰《列女後傳》七十二人，雜論議、詩賦、碑頌、駁難十餘萬言，喪亂盡失。

translations.literal: Also he compiled Continued Biographies of Exemplary Women seventy-two persons, miscellaneous discourses, rhapsodies, stele eulogics, and refutations over one hundred thousand graphs; in mourning turmoil all was lost.
translations.idiomatic: He also wrote seventy-two further exemplary women's lives and well over a hundred thousand characters of essays, verse, inscriptions, and polemics—all lost in the wars.

sentences.zh: 長子愆期，流寓江南，緣父本意，更注《公羊》，又集《列女後傳》云。

translations.literal: The eldest son Qianqi drifted lodged south of the river; following his father's original intent, he again annotated Gongyang, and also gathered Continued Biographies of Exemplary Women.
translations.idiomatic: His eldest son Qianqi, exiled south of the Yangzi, re-edited the Gongyang commentary in his father's spirit and reassembled the sequel to Exemplary Women.

sentences.zh: 【史評】

translations.literal: Historian's judgment
translations.idiomatic: Court historian's verdict

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：皇甫謐素履幽貞，閒居養疾，留情筆削，敦悅丘墳，軒冕未足為榮，貧賤不以為恥，確乎不拔，斯固有晉之高人者歟！

translations.literal: The court historian says: Huangfu Mi in plain tread was darkly chaste; idle residence nurtured illness; he placed feeling in brush-cutting; earnestly delighted in mounds and tombs; tall caps and tethered ribbons were not enough to be glory; poverty and low status he did not take as shame; firmly unmoved—thus is he indeed a lofty man of Jin!
translations.idiomatic: The historians praise Huangfu Mi for living plainly in seclusion, tending chronic illness while devoting himself to scholarship; rank could not tempt him and want could not shame him—an unbending Jin exemplar of the first rank.

sentences.zh: 洎乎《篤終》立論，薄葬昭儉，既戒奢于季氏，亦無取于王孫，可謂達存亡之機矣。

translations.literal: Down to when Sincere to the End set up argument, thin burial illuminated frugality; already warning luxury in the Ji clan, also having nothing to take from Prince Yang of Wei; it can be called grasping the pivot of survival and death.
translations.idiomatic: His essay Sincere to the End preached modest burial, warning against the Jis' extravagance without copying Yang Wangsun's naked interment—altogether a balanced grasp of how to meet mortality.

sentences.zh: 摯虞、束皙等並詳覽載籍，多識舊章，奏議可觀，文詞雅贍，可謂博聞之士也。

translations.literal: Zhi Yu, Shu Xi, and others together broadly perused carried texts, much knew old patterns; their memorials and deliberations were worth viewing, literary phrasing elegant and rich—they may be called men of broad hearing.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi Yu and Shu Xi, steeped in the archives, wrote lucid memorials and graceful prose—true scholars of wide learning.

sentences.zh: 或攝官延閣，裁成言事之書；

translations.literal: Some held office in the extended pavilion, trimmed and completed books that set forth affairs;
translations.idiomatic: Some served in the imperial library and edited state papers;

sentences.zh: 或蒞政秩宗，參定禋郊之禮。

translations.literal: some attended government as Minister of Rites, joined in fixing suburban sacrifice ritual.
translations.idiomatic: others directed the ministry of rites and helped shape the suburban cult.

sentences.zh: 虞既厄於從理，皙乃年位不充，天之報施，何其爽也！

translations.literal: Yu already was blocked by following principle; Xi then in years and rank was not filled—Heaven’s requital and bestowal, how uneven it is!
translations.idiomatic: Zhi Yu was thwarted by his own integrity; Shu Xi died before his talents ripened—how uneven Heaven’s rewards can be!

sentences.zh: 王接才調秀出，見賞知音，惜其夭枉，未申驥足，嗟夫！

translations.literal: Wang Jie’s talent and tune stood out; he was prized by one who knew the tone; pity his early cut-off, not extending the thoroughbred’s hooves—alas!
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jie’s gifts shone and won a patron’s praise, yet he died young before his stride could open—alas!

sentences.zh: 贊曰：士安好逸，棲心蓬蓽。

translations.literal: The encomium says: Shi’an loved ease; his heart lodged in brushwood and thatch.
translations.idiomatic: Encomium: Master Shi’an chose ease and a thatched heart.

sentences.zh: 屬意文雅，忘懷榮秩。

translations.literal: He set intent on literary refinement, forgot rank and stipend.
translations.idiomatic: He lived for letters and forgot ambition for office.

sentences.zh: 遺制可稱，養生乖術。

translations.literal: His dying instructions could be praised; nurturing life, he missed the art.
translations.idiomatic: His testament commands respect, though his quest for long life misfired.

sentences.zh: 摯虞博聞，廣微絕群。

translations.literal: Zhi Yu heard widely; Guangwei stood apart from the crowd.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi Yu was encyclopedic; Shu Xi, “Guangwei,” stood alone.

sentences.zh: 財成禮度，刊緝遺文。

translations.literal: They trimmed and completed ritual measures, carved and compiled lost texts.
translations.idiomatic: They shaped ritual codes and edited lost classics.

sentences.zh: 魏篇式序，漢冊斯分。

translations.literal: Wei’s chapters gained order; Han’s registers were thus divided.
translations.idiomatic: They set Wei literature in order and sorted the Han corpus.

sentences.zh: 祖遊後出，亦播清芬。

translations.literal: Zu You afterward came forth, also spreading clear fragrance.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jie followed later and left a clean name as well.
